input:
Write a bash script that converts a CSV file to JSON Lines.

Starting files:
--- /home/eval/data/users.csv (no trailing newline on the last line) ---
id,name,email,active
1,Alice Smith,alice@example.com,yes
2,Bob Jones,bob@example.com,no
3,Carol White,carol@example.com,yes
--- end ---

Fields never contain commas or quotes.

Write /home/eval/data/users.jsonl with one compact JSON object per data row (no spaces), in input order, keys in this order: `id` (JSON number), `name` (string), `email` (string), `active` (JSON boolean: `yes` -> true, anything else -> false). Example line: `{"id":1,"name":"Alice Smith","email":"alice@example.com","active":true}`. Every row must be converted, including the last one.

Then print `active=<number of active users>` to stdout and exit 0.

transcript.final_response:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
INPUT="/home/eval/data/users.csv"
OUTPUT="/home/eval/data/users.jsonl"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUTPUT")"
: > "$OUTPUT"
active_count=0
first=1
while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
  line=${line%$'\r'}
  if (( first )); then
    first=0
    continue
  fi
  [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
  IFS=, read -r id name email active <<< "$line"
  active=${active%$'\r'}
  if [[ "$active" == "yes" ]]; then
    bool="true"
    active_count=$((active_count + 1))
  else
    bool="false"
  fi
  printf '{"id":%s,"name":"%s","email":"%s","active":%s}\n' "$id" "$name" "$email" "$bool" >> "$OUTPUT"
done < "$INPUT"
echo "active=$active_count"
exit 0
```
